questions.stem: Values can best be described as
options: the amount of money a person has saved in the bank
the rules made by the National Assembly
the beliefs and ideas a person or society holds as important and worthwhile
the prices of goods in the market
questions.explanation: Values are the things we believe are good, right and important, and they guide how we behave.

questions.stem: Values show themselves at two main levels. These are the
options: federal level and the state level
individual level and the society level
rural level and the urban level
primary level and the secondary level
questions.explanation: A person has personal values, and a whole society also shares common values.

questions.stem: Which of the following factors helps to promote a good value system in a community?
options: Favouring only one's relatives in sharing benefits
Treating people differently because of their tribe
Breaking promises whenever it is convenient
Consistency, trust and fairness among members
questions.explanation: A value system grows when people are consistent, trust one another and treat others fairly.

questions.stem: One importance of shared values in a society is that they
options: encourage people to disobey the law
make people suspicious of their neighbours
questions.explanation: When people share good values, they live together in unity and peace.

questions.stem: A person who tells the truth and does not cheat or steal is said to be
questions.explanation: Honesty means being truthful and fair in what we say and do.

questions.stem: Chiamaka found a purse containing ₦5,000 on the school corridor and took it to the principal's office. Chiamaka has shown the value of
questions.explanation: Returning what does not belong to you is a clear act of honesty.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a consequence of examination malpractice for a student who is caught?
options: The student's result may be cancelled and the student punished
The student is automatically promoted to the next class
The student is given a scholarship by the government
The student becomes more respected by teachers
questions.explanation: Exam cheating is dishonest; it can lead to cancelled results, suspension or other punishment.

questions.stem: A trader in Onitsha market tampers with his measuring tin so that customers get less garri than they pay for. In the long run, the most likely result of this dishonesty is that
options: the government will give him an award
customers will lose trust in him and stop buying from him
other traders will lower their prices to match his
his business will grow because customers like small measures
questions.explanation: Dishonesty destroys trust, and a trader who is not trusted soon loses customers.

questions.stem: Working together with others to achieve a common goal is called
questions.explanation: Cooperation means people joining hands to work towards the same goal.

questions.stem: Which of these is an attribute of cooperation?
options: Laughing at the mistakes of others
questions.explanation: Cooperative people share, care for and support one another.

questions.stem: The people of a village in Ekiti State came together on a Saturday to clear the road leading to their market. This activity shows cooperation, and its main benefit to the village is
options: more work for only one family
the loss of the village market
an increase in quarrels among villagers
faster progress in achieving a common goal
questions.explanation: When people cooperate, they achieve goals such as a clean road faster and more cheaply.

questions.stem: Which of the following factors is most likely to PROMOTE cooperation among students in a class?
questions.explanation: Respect and good communication help people to trust each other and work together.

questions.stem: Self-reliance means
options: depending on one's own abilities and resources to meet one's needs
waiting for the government to provide all needs
depending on others for everything one needs
questions.explanation: A self-reliant person uses his or her own skills and effort to take care of needs.

questions.stem: Tunde discovered that he is good at drawing. He joined the art club and practised every week until he could design posters for sale. The steps Tunde followed are
options: borrowing, begging and spending his talent
identifying, nurturing and perfecting his talent
copying, cheating and selling his talent
hiding, ignoring and abandoning his talent
questions.explanation: Talents must first be discovered, then developed and finally perfected through practice.

questions.stem: The wealth of a nation is found mainly in its
questions.explanation: A nation becomes wealthy by using its natural resources and the skills of its people.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most likely consequence for a country when the talents of its young people are not discovered or developed?
options: High unemployment and slow national development
A reduction in poverty and crime
A rise in the number of skilled workers
questions.explanation: Undeveloped talents mean fewer skilled people, more unemployment and slower progress.

questions.stem: A person who keeps to strong moral principles even when nobody is watching is said to have
questions.explanation: Integrity means doing what is right at all times, whether or not anyone is watching.

questions.stem: A cashier refused a bribe of ₦20,000 offered to him to pay out money without proper documents. This shows that the cashier is a person of
questions.explanation: Refusing to do wrong for personal gain shows integrity.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements best describes the relationship between integrity and trust in public office?
options: Leaders with integrity lose the trust of citizens because they are too strict
Citizens trust leaders more when they make promises they do not keep
Integrity has nothing to do with how much citizens trust their leaders
Leaders with integrity earn the trust of citizens because their actions match their words
questions.explanation: People trust leaders whose words and actions agree; that consistency is integrity.

questions.stem: Being satisfied with what one has and not envying others is called
questions.explanation: Contentment means being happy with what you have.

questions.stem: Which of the following behaviours shows that a student is NOT contented?
options: Stealing a classmate's new phone because he wants one
Saving his pocket money to buy a book
Thanking his parents for his school sandals
Using his old school bag carefully
questions.explanation: Taking what belongs to others because you want it shows lack of contentment.

questions.stem: One benefit of contentment to the society is that it
options: makes people envious of their neighbours
encourages people to live above their income
questions.explanation: Contented people do not steal or take bribes to get what others have.

questions.stem: Discipline can be described as
options: obeying rules only when a teacher is watching
being satisfied with whatever one already has
training oneself to obey rules and control one's behaviour
punishing other people whenever they make mistakes
questions.explanation: Discipline is self-control and obedience to rules.

questions.stem: Which of these is a sign of a disciplined student?
options: Coming to school early and obeying school rules
Leaving school before closing time without permission
questions.explanation: A disciplined student keeps rules, is punctual and controls his or her actions.

questions.stem: A school prefect who punishes other students for lateness but always comes late himself is showing
questions.explanation: Discipline starts with oneself; a leader who breaks the rule he enforces lacks self-discipline.

questions.stem: Courage is the ability to
options: be satisfied with what one has in life
work together with others to achieve a goal
obey every instruction without asking any questions
face danger, pain or difficulty without being overcome by fear
questions.explanation: A courageous person faces difficult situations bravely.

questions.stem: Amina told her teacher about a group of students planning to bully a junior student, even though they threatened her. Amina has shown
questions.explanation: Standing up for what is right in spite of threats is courage.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the BEST example of moral courage?
options: Climbing the school's water tank to win a bet
Crossing a busy expressway to impress classmates
Fighting a senior student who insulted your friend
Refusing to cheat in an examination although friends mock you
questions.explanation: Moral courage means doing what is right even when it is unpopular; showing off or fighting is not courage.

questions.topic: National Values: Right Attitude to Work
questions.stem: Right attitude to work means
options: coming to work only when one feels like it
doing as little work as possible for the same pay
having a positive and responsible approach to one's duties
using office time for personal business
questions.explanation: A right attitude to work is being committed, honest and responsible in one's job.

questions.topic: National Values: Right Attitude to Work
questions.stem: Which of the following is an attribute of right attitude to work?
questions.explanation: Being on time (punctuality) is a key part of right attitude to work.

questions.topic: National Values: Right Attitude to Work
questions.stem: Rewarding hard-working staff in an organisation is important mainly because it
options: reduces the quality of goods produced
questions.explanation: Rewards motivate workers to do more and better work.

questions.topic: National Values: Right Attitude to Work
questions.stem: A mechanic who fails to tighten the brakes of a commercial bus properly before handing it back to the driver may cause
options: an increase in the number of passengers
a road accident that leads to loss of lives
a reduction in the price of fuel
questions.explanation: Careless work, such as poor vehicle repair, can cause national disasters like road accidents.

questions.topic: National Values: Right Attitude to Work
questions.stem: Which of the following is the most likely consequence for a nation when many civil servants lack the right attitude to work?
options: Better health care and quicker services
Declining productivity and poor public services
Rapid economic growth and full employment
questions.explanation: Lazy or dishonest workers reduce productivity and services become poor.

questions.stem: Behaviour that is harmful to oneself or the society and is against accepted values is called
questions.explanation: Negative behaviour goes against the good values of society.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of negative behaviour?
questions.explanation: Cultism is a negative behaviour that leads to violence and fear.

questions.stem: Living a very flashy life, such as buying expensive cars just to show off wealth whose source is unknown, is known as
questions.explanation: Ostentatious living means showing off wealth in a wasteful way.

questions.stem: One major effect of negative behaviour on the society is
questions.explanation: Negative behaviours like dishonesty and cultism increase crime in society.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the MOST effective way of promoting positive behaviour among young people?
options: Rewarding good conduct and showing good examples by parents and leaders
Celebrating people who become rich quickly through fraud
Encouraging students to join secret cults for protection
questions.explanation: Young people learn by example and respond to rewards for good conduct.

questions.stem: When people in a society no longer value hard work and honesty but admire anyone who has money no matter how it was made, the society is suffering from
questions.explanation: Value disorientation is when good values are abandoned and wrong values are admired.

questions.stem: Citizenship can be defined as
options: the legal status of being a full member of a country
the right to travel to any country without a passport
the act of living in a city
questions.explanation: Citizenship is the legal membership of a country, with rights and duties.

questions.stem: A child born in Kano to Nigerian parents is a Nigerian citizen by
questions.explanation: Being born to Nigerian parents gives citizenship by birth.

questions.stem: A foreign woman who marries a Nigerian man may become a Nigerian citizen by
questions.explanation: The Nigerian constitution allows a foreign woman married to a Nigerian man to become a citizen by registration.

questions.stem: A foreigner who has lived in Nigeria for many years, is of good character and applies to the government to become a Nigerian, becomes a citizen by
questions.explanation: Naturalisation is the process by which a foreigner who meets the legal conditions is granted citizenship.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a usual requirement for a foreigner seeking Nigerian citizenship by naturalisation?
options: Being a member of a political party
Showing a clear intention to live in Nigeria
Having lived in Nigeria for the required number of years
questions.explanation: Political party membership is not a condition for naturalisation; good character, residence and intention to stay are.

questions.topic: Rights and Duties of a Citizen
questions.stem: The things a citizen is entitled to enjoy from the state are called
questions.explanation: Rights are freedoms and benefits a citizen is entitled to.

questions.topic: Rights and Duties of a Citizen
questions.stem: Which of the following is a duty of a Nigerian citizen?
questions.explanation: Paying tax is something a citizen must do; the others are rights.

questions.topic: Rights and Duties of a Citizen
questions.stem: The main difference between rights and duties is that
options: rights are given only to adults, while duties are for children
rights are what citizens enjoy, while duties are what citizens are expected to do
rights are paid for, while duties are free
rights are found in the Bible, while duties are found in the Quran
questions.explanation: Rights are entitlements; duties are obligations to the state and society.

questions.topic: Rights and Duties of a Citizen
questions.stem: When citizens perform their duties and respect the rights of others, the society enjoys
questions.explanation: Respect for rights and duties brings social control, peace and discipline.

questions.topic: Rights and Duties of a Citizen
questions.stem: Bola says she has the right to play loud music at midnight in her compound. Her neighbours complain that they cannot sleep. This situation shows that
options: neighbours have no rights in their homes
rights have no limits at all
only the government can play music at night
rights must be exercised without violating the rights of others
questions.explanation: Every right has limits; it should not be used in a way that harms other people's rights.

questions.stem: The supremacy of the constitution means that
options: state laws are higher than the constitution
the constitution is the highest law of the land
the constitution can be ignored during elections
the President is above the constitution
questions.explanation: No law or person is above the constitution; it is the supreme law.

questions.stem: If a State House of Assembly passes a law that conflicts with the Nigerian constitution, that law will be
options: sent to the Queen of England for approval
void to the extent of its inconsistency
questions.explanation: Any law that conflicts with the constitution is void to the extent of the conflict.

questions.stem: Which body has the power to declare that a law is unconstitutional in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The judiciary interprets the constitution and can declare a law unconstitutional.

questions.stem: A constitution is
options: the yearly budget presented by the President
a body of rules and principles by which a country is governed
a list of decrees made by traditional rulers
a collection of bye-laws made by a local government
questions.explanation: A constitution contains the basic rules for governing a country.

questions.stem: The first constitution of colonial Nigeria that introduced the elective principle was the
questions.explanation: The Clifford Constitution of 1922 first allowed some members of the Legislative Council to be elected.

questions.stem: Under the Clifford Constitution of 1922, the elective principle allowed people in
options: Ibadan only to elect the Sultan
all Nigerian towns to elect the Prime Minister
Lagos and Calabar to elect members of the Legislative Council
Kano and Sokoto to elect the Governor
questions.explanation: Only Lagos and Calabar had elected members under the Clifford Constitution.

questions.stem: The colonial constitution that divided Nigeria into three regions (Northern, Western and Eastern) was the
questions.explanation: The Richards Constitution introduced regionalism with three regions.

questions.stem: The constitution that first made Nigeria a federation was the
questions.explanation: The Lyttelton Constitution of 1954 introduced a federal system of government.

questions.stem: Which of the following constitutions made Nigeria a republic, with a Nigerian as ceremonial President in place of the British monarch?
questions.explanation: The 1963 Republican Constitution removed the British monarch as Nigeria's head of state.

questions.stem: The 1979 Constitution of Nigeria is remembered mainly for introducing
options: the regional system with three regions
the elective principle for Lagos and Calabar
questions.explanation: The 1979 Constitution replaced the parliamentary system with a presidential system.

questions.stem: The Macpherson Constitution of 1951 differed from earlier colonial constitutions because
options: it made Nigeria an independent country
Nigerians were widely consulted before it was drawn up
it was written without any Nigerian input
questions.explanation: The Macpherson Constitution was the first made after wide consultation with Nigerians.

questions.stem: The colours of the Nigerian national flag are
questions.explanation: The Nigerian flag has three vertical stripes: green, white and green.

questions.stem: In the Nigerian national flag, the green colour stands for
questions.explanation: Green represents Nigeria's agriculture and rich land, while white represents peace and unity.

questions.stem: On the Nigerian coat of arms, the eagle represents
questions.explanation: The eagle on the coat of arms stands for strength.

questions.stem: On the Nigerian coat of arms, the white wavy Y-shaped band on the black shield represents
questions.explanation: The Y-shape shows where the rivers Niger and Benue meet; the black shield stands for the fertile soil.

questions.stem: The motto on the Nigerian coat of arms is
options: Unity and Faith, Peace and Progress
questions.explanation: The national motto is 'Unity and Faith, Peace and Progress'.

questions.stem: The National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) was established mainly to
options: train young graduates to serve in the armed forces
promote national unity among young graduates
provide paid jobs for all graduates permanently
questions.explanation: NYSC posts graduates to states other than their own to promote unity and understanding.

questions.stem: The 'Federal Character' principle in Nigeria is meant to ensure that
options: appointments into public offices reflect the diversity of the states and peoples of Nigeria
only people from the Federal Capital Territory are employed by government
every state has its own army
federal roads are built in only one region
questions.explanation: Federal Character spreads public jobs and positions fairly among people from all parts of Nigeria.

questions.stem: Federal Government Colleges (Unity Schools) help to promote national unity mainly by
options: giving free university places to all their students
teaching students in only the language of the host state
admitting students from different states and ethnic groups to learn together
admitting only students whose parents work for government
questions.explanation: Unity Schools bring students from all parts of Nigeria together so they grow up as friends.

questions.stem: Which of these practices would BEST promote national unity in Nigeria?
options: Mocking the languages of other tribes
Tolerance of other people's culture and religion
Hiring workers only from one's own ethnic group
questions.explanation: Tolerance and non-discrimination help different groups to live in unity.

questions.stem: A federation is a system of government in which
options: the President makes all laws without a legislature
all powers are held by one central government only
the states are fully independent countries with their own armies
powers are shared between a central government and component units such as states
questions.explanation: In a federation, powers are shared between the centre and the states by the constitution.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a reason why Nigeria adopted federalism?
options: To make every state independent of the centre
To remove the need for a written constitution
To allow unity in diversity among its many ethnic groups
To give the largest region control over the others
questions.explanation: Federalism lets many different peoples remain united while managing some of their own affairs.

questions.stem: One characteristic of a federation is that
options: the central government cannot make any laws
there is a written constitution that shares powers between levels of government
there is only one level of government
the states can leave the federation at any time without law
questions.explanation: A federation needs a written constitution that clearly shares powers.

questions.stem: Nigeria is made up of
options: 12 states and the Federal Capital Territory
36 states and the Federal Capital Territory
questions.explanation: Nigeria has 36 states plus the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja.

questions.topic: Relationship Between Federal, State and Local Governments
questions.stem: The three tiers of government in Nigeria are
questions.explanation: Nigeria's three tiers (levels) are federal, state and local government.

questions.topic: Relationship Between Federal, State and Local Governments
questions.stem: Matters on which ONLY the federal government can make laws are listed in the
questions.explanation: The Exclusive List contains matters like defence and currency that only the federal government handles.

questions.topic: Relationship Between Federal, State and Local Governments
questions.stem: Which of the following is on the Concurrent Legislative List, where both federal and state governments can make laws?
questions.explanation: Education is a concurrent matter; defence, currency and foreign affairs are exclusive to the federal government.

questions.topic: Relationship Between Federal, State and Local Governments
questions.stem: Which of these is a function of a local government council?
questions.explanation: Local governments handle local matters like birth and death registration, markets and motor parks.

questions.topic: Relationship Between Federal, State and Local Governments
questions.stem: Matters that are not on either the Exclusive or the Concurrent List and are left for states to handle are called
questions.explanation: Residual matters are the remaining powers left to the states.

questions.topic: Relationship Between Federal, State and Local Governments
questions.stem: The law-making body of a local government council in Nigeria is made up of
options: members of the House of Representatives
questions.explanation: Elected councillors make bye-laws for the local government.

questions.stem: The rule of law means that
options: people in power can change the law whenever they like
laws apply mainly to ordinary citizens and not to leaders
the police alone decide who has broken the law
everybody, including leaders, is subject to the law of the land
questions.explanation: Under the rule of law, no one is above the law.

questions.stem: A law can be defined as
options: a binding rule made by a recognised authority
a promise made by a politician during campaigns
a custom observed only during festivals
a piece of advice people may follow if they wish
questions.explanation: Laws are binding rules made by a proper authority, with punishment for breaking them.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a principle of the rule of law?
options: Equality of all citizens before the law
Detention of citizens without any charge
questions.explanation: Everyone is equal before the law, whether rich or poor, leader or follower.

questions.stem: The opposite of the rule of law, where a ruler acts according to personal wishes rather than the law, is called
questions.explanation: Arbitrary rule means governing by personal will instead of by law.

questions.stem: A man was arrested for stealing a goat and was beaten and locked up for three months without being taken to court. Which principle of the rule of law was violated?
questions.explanation: An accused person must be brought before a court and given a fair hearing within a reasonable time.

questions.topic: Protection of Human Rights and the Rule of Law
questions.stem: Which of the following can help to protect the human rights of a citizen whose rights have been violated?
options: Fighting the offender in the street
questions.explanation: The courts are the main place to seek protection when rights are violated.

questions.topic: Protection of Human Rights and the Rule of Law
questions.stem: The government agency that provides free legal services to poor Nigerians who cannot afford a lawyer is the
questions.explanation: The Legal Aid Council helps poor people get lawyers to defend their rights.

questions.topic: Protection of Human Rights and the Rule of Law
questions.stem: Civil society organisations protect human rights mainly by
options: trying and sentencing those who violate rights
making laws for the protection of citizens
drawing public attention to rights violations and defending victims
questions.explanation: Civil society groups speak out, use the media and support victims of rights abuse.

questions.topic: Protection of Human Rights and the Rule of Law
questions.stem: Which of the following is a PEACEFUL way of drawing attention to cases of human rights violation?
options: Media reports and peaceful protest marches
questions.explanation: Peaceful protests and media reports draw attention without breaking the law.

questions.stem: A consumer is a person who
options: buys and uses goods and services
questions.explanation: Anyone who buys or uses goods and services is a consumer.

questions.stem: Ngozi bought a new fan with a one-year warranty, and it stopped working after two months. Her right to have the fan repaired or replaced is the right to
questions.explanation: The right to redress means a consumer can get compensation for faulty goods.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a responsibility of a consumer?
options: Demanding and keeping receipts for goods bought
Throwing refuse on the road after shopping
Buying goods without checking expiry dates
questions.explanation: Keeping receipts gives proof of a transaction if something goes wrong.

questions.stem: The right of consumers to know the ingredients, price and expiry date of a product is called the right to
questions.explanation: Consumers have a right to accurate information about what they buy.

questions.stem: Democracy is often described as government
options: of the rich, by the rich and for the rich
of the people, by the people and for the people
of the soldiers, by the soldiers and for the soldiers
questions.explanation: This popular definition shows that power belongs to the people in a democracy.

questions.stem: Which of these is a feature of democracy?
questions.explanation: Regular elections let people choose and change their leaders.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a democratic institution in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: INEC, political parties and the arms of government are democratic institutions.

questions.stem: The three arms of government in a democracy are the
questions.explanation: The legislature makes laws, the executive carries them out and the judiciary interprets them.

questions.stem: Groups of people who try to influence government policies without seeking to form a government themselves are called
questions.explanation: Pressure groups, such as trade unions, influence policy but do not contest elections.

questions.stem: The pillars of democracy are
options: the tall columns in the National Assembly building
the basic elements that support and sustain democracy
the soldiers who guard the President
questions.explanation: Pillars of democracy are the key things that hold democracy up.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a pillar of democracy?
options: Control of the press by the government
Majority rule with respect for minority rights
questions.explanation: Democracy rests on majority rule while protecting the rights of the minority.

questions.stem: Why is a transparent electoral process regarded as a pillar of democracy?
options: It removes the need for political parties
It gives the military the power to choose leaders
It allows the winner to be decided before voting
It ensures that leaders truly represent the choice of the people
questions.explanation: A transparent process makes sure the people's real choice wins.

questions.stem: An election is
options: the process of appointing a king
the process of choosing leaders by voting
the act of forcing people into office
questions.explanation: In an election, citizens choose their leaders by casting votes.

questions.stem: In Nigeria, the minimum age for a person to register and vote is
questions.explanation: A Nigerian citizen must be at least 18 years old to vote.

questions.stem: An election held to fill a vacant seat when an elected member dies or resigns before the end of the term is called a
questions.explanation: A bye-election fills a seat that becomes vacant in the middle of a term.

questions.stem: An election in which members of a political party choose their candidate for a general election is called a
questions.explanation: Party primaries are used to pick the party's candidate.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a responsibility of a good voter?
options: Selling his or her voter's card to the highest bidder
Voting more than once to help a favourite candidate
Destroying ballot boxes when his candidate is losing
Voting according to his or her conscience without collecting bribes
questions.explanation: A responsible voter votes freely and honestly and refuses inducement.

questions.stem: A vote in which citizens are asked to decide directly on an important issue, rather than to choose a candidate, is called a
questions.explanation: In a referendum, citizens vote 'yes' or 'no' on an issue.

questions.stem: Electoral malpractice means
options: the campaigning of candidates before an election
illegal or dishonest acts done to influence the outcome of an election
the legal process of registering and voting in an election
the counting and announcing of results by electoral officers
questions.explanation: Electoral malpractice is cheating or wrongdoing in elections.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a form of electoral malpractice?
options: Checking one's name on the register
questions.explanation: Voting more than once is illegal.

questions.stem: A politician who gives voters bags of rice and money on election day so that they vote for him is guilty of
questions.explanation: Giving gifts to influence votes is vote buying, a form of electoral malpractice.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most serious effect of electoral malpractice on a democracy?
options: More citizens trust the electoral process
Political parties become stronger and more honest
Leaders who were not truly chosen by the people come to power
questions.explanation: When elections are rigged, the people's true choice is denied and democracy is weakened.

questions.topic: Elections and Electoral Bodies in Nigeria
questions.stem: The body responsible for conducting federal and state elections in Nigeria is the
questions.explanation: INEC conducts presidential, governorship and National and State Assembly elections.

questions.topic: Elections and Electoral Bodies in Nigeria
questions.stem: Local government elections in a Nigerian state are conducted by the
questions.explanation: Each state's SIEC conducts local government council elections.

questions.topic: Elections and Electoral Bodies in Nigeria
questions.stem: Free and fair elections are needed mainly because they
options: make it easy for thugs to win
allow results to be written before voting
keep citizens away from polling units
questions.explanation: Leaders chosen in free and fair elections are accepted as lawful by the people.

questions.topic: Elections and Electoral Bodies in Nigeria
questions.stem: Which of the following is the BEST way to prevent electoral malpractice in Nigeria?
options: Strict punishment of offenders and voter education
questions.explanation: Educating voters and punishing those who cheat discourage malpractice.

questions.stem: Voting is
options: the act of expressing one's choice in an election
the act of buying a voter's card
the act of campaigning for a party
questions.explanation: Voting is how citizens express their choice of leaders.

questions.stem: Before a Nigerian can vote in an election, he or she must first
questions.explanation: Only registered voters can vote.

questions.stem: The method of voting in which voters mark their ballot papers privately so that no one knows whom they voted for is called
questions.explanation: Secret ballot protects voters from intimidation.

questions.stem: Arrange the following steps of voting at a polling unit in the correct order: (i) the voter thumbprints the ballot paper in secret; (ii) the voter's card is checked and accredited; (iii) the ballot paper is dropped in the ballot box; (iv) the voter is given a ballot paper.
questions.explanation: A voter is first accredited, then given a ballot paper, marks it in secret and drops it in the box.

questions.stem: A crime is
options: an act that breaks the law and is punishable by the state
any act that makes a person happy
a mistake in a mathematics test
a quarrel between two friends that is settled at home
questions.explanation: A crime is an offence against the law that attracts punishment.

questions.stem: Obtaining money from people by deceiving them with false promises, popularly called '419', is known as
questions.explanation: 419 is advance fee fraud, named after a section of the Nigerian Criminal Code.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a common cause of crime among young people?
questions.explanation: Idleness and lack of jobs can push young people into crime.

questions.stem: One effect of a high crime rate in a community is that
options: investors are afraid to set up businesses there
people sleep with their doors open
questions.explanation: Crime makes an area unsafe and drives away investors and visitors.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the BEST way for a community to prevent crime?
options: Taking the law into their own hands by lynching suspects
Cooperating with security agents through neighbourhood watch and quick reporting
questions.explanation: Crime prevention works best when citizens work with security agencies.

questions.stem: If you see a suspicious bag left unattended at a motor park, the best thing to do is to
options: move away and report it to security officials immediately
open it carefully to find the owner's address
ask a friend to help you move it aside
take it to the nearest shop for safekeeping
questions.explanation: Never touch suspicious objects; move away and report to security officials.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the national emergency telephone number that can be dialled in Nigeria to report a crime or emergency?
questions.explanation: 112 is Nigeria's toll-free national emergency number.

questions.stem: When reporting a crime to the police, which of the following information is most useful?
options: The time, place and what happened
A guess about the suspect's motive
questions.explanation: Clear details of time, place and people help the police to act quickly.

questions.stem: Kemi noticed that a stranger had been watching the gate of her school every afternoon and trying to talk to young pupils. The most appropriate response is to
options: post his picture on social media with insults
ignore the stranger because he has not done anything yet
inform the school authorities and her parents so they can alert security agents
confront the stranger alone and warn him to leave
questions.explanation: Suspicious behaviour should be reported to responsible adults who can involve security agents.

questions.stem: In Nigeria, the punishment for a person found guilty of murder can be
questions.explanation: Murder is a very serious crime and can attract the death penalty under Nigerian law.

questions.stem: Selling food that has been mixed with harmful substances is known as
questions.explanation: Adding harmful substances to food makes it contaminated and dangerous.

questions.stem: Drug adulteration means
options: giving a drug a new brand name
taking a drug as the doctor prescribed
mixing a drug with fake or impure substances
storing a drug at the right temperature
questions.explanation: Adulterated drugs are impure or fake and can kill instead of cure.

questions.stem: Which of the following crimes is most commonly punished by imprisonment in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Theft is a criminal offence punishable by imprisonment; the others are not crimes.

questions.stem: Emergency management means
options: the daily running of a business
preparing for and responding to sudden dangers
treating patients in a hospital ward
questions.explanation: Emergency management is preparing for and responding to sudden dangers.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of an emergency?
questions.explanation: A building collapse is a sudden, dangerous event that needs urgent action.

questions.stem: When a person's clothes catch fire, the person should
options: stop, drop to the ground and roll
fan the flames with a cloth
questions.explanation: Running fans the flames; stopping, dropping and rolling helps to put the fire out.

questions.stem: The federal agency responsible for coordinating responses to disasters such as floods in Nigeria is the
options: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC)
questions.explanation: NEMA coordinates disaster management at the national level.

questions.stem: A classmate collapses after eating food bought from an unknown roadside seller and starts vomiting. The best immediate response is to
options: pour cold water on the classmate's head and walk away
give the classmate more of the same food
call a teacher and take the classmate to the nearest health centre at once
leave the classmate alone to sleep it off
questions.explanation: Suspected food poisoning needs quick medical attention.

questions.stem: National security means
options: the number of soldiers in the armed forces
protecting the nation and its people from threats
questions.explanation: National security is about keeping the country and its people safe.

questions.stem: Breaking oil pipelines to steal petroleum products is known as
questions.explanation: Pipeline vandalism damages the economy and the environment and threatens security.

questions.stem: Which of the following crimes MOST directly threatens national security?
questions.explanation: Terrorism uses violence to cause fear and directly threatens the nation's safety.

questions.stem: Illegal oil bunkering affects Nigeria's national security mainly because it
options: it reduces revenue and funds criminal groups
it increases the price of school uniforms
it creates more jobs in the civil service
questions.explanation: Stolen oil money funds crime, government loses revenue and spills damage the land and water.

questions.topic: History of Nigerian Social Studies Education
questions.stem: Social Studies was first introduced as a school subject in Nigeria at
questions.explanation: Aiyetoro Comprehensive High School pioneered Social Studies in Nigeria in the 1960s.

questions.topic: History of Nigerian Social Studies Education
questions.stem: The National Curriculum Conference held in Lagos in 1969 was important to Social Studies because it
options: abolished the teaching of History and Geography in all schools
recommended a curriculum that would make education relevant to Nigerian needs
made Social Studies a university subject only
introduced the 6-3-3-4 system in the same year
questions.explanation: The 1969 conference called for education relevant to Nigeria's needs, which supported Social Studies.

questions.topic: History of Nigerian Social Studies Education
questions.stem: Social Studies was introduced into the Nigerian school curriculum mainly to
options: replace Mathematics and English as core subjects
teach students about the history of Europe
prepare students mainly for jobs in other countries
help learners understand their society and become good citizens
questions.explanation: Social Studies helps young people understand their environment and society.

questions.topic: History of Nigerian Social Studies Education
questions.stem: Before Social Studies was introduced, Nigerian schools taught separate subjects such as History, Geography and Civics. Social Studies differs from them because it
options: concentrates on physical features like rivers and mountains
integrates ideas from several subjects to study man and his environment as a whole
deals only with the laws and constitution of Nigeria
studies only past events in Nigerian history
questions.explanation: Social Studies is integrated: it combines ideas from many subjects to study man in his environment.

questions.stem: One general objective of Social Studies is to
options: prepare students mainly for careers abroad
develop good citizens who can contribute to the development of society
teach students to be loyal only to their ethnic groups
train students to pass only external examinations
questions.explanation: Social Studies aims to raise responsible citizens.

questions.stem: Social Studies helps learners to develop national consciousness, which means
options: interest in leaving Nigeria for other countries
knowledge of the history of foreign countries
awareness of being a Nigerian and love for the country
loyalty to one's ethnic group above the nation
questions.explanation: National consciousness is the feeling of belonging to and caring about Nigeria.

questions.stem: Which objective of Social Studies is shown when a student learns to cope with changes such as moving from a village to a city?
questions.explanation: Social Studies helps learners adjust to changes in their environment.

questions.stem: Which of the following best shows that Social Studies has achieved its objective of inculcating the right values and attitudes?
options: A student who refuses to work with classmates from other states
A student who scores high marks by copying from others
A student who destroys school property during a protest
A student who returns lost property and respects people of other ethnic groups
questions.explanation: Right values show in honest, respectful and tolerant behaviour.

questions.stem: The contents of Social Studies include facts, concepts, skills, values and
questions.explanation: Social Studies content covers facts, concepts, skills, values and attitudes.

questions.stem: The part of Social Studies content that deals with knowledge and thinking is called the
questions.explanation: The cognitive domain is about knowing and thinking.

questions.stem: The affective content of Social Studies deals mainly with
questions.explanation: Affective content is about feelings, values and attitudes.

questions.stem: A Social Studies lesson in which students practise drawing a sketch map of their school compound mainly develops the
questions.explanation: Using the hands to carry out a skill belongs to the psychomotor domain.

questions.stem: A primary group is a social group in which members
options: relate mainly through written rules and offices
have close, personal and face-to-face relationships
questions.explanation: Primary groups like the family have close, intimate relationships.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the best example of a primary group?
questions.explanation: The family is the most basic primary group.

questions.stem: The family is regarded as a primary group because
options: members have close and lasting relationships
members are bound by a written constitution
it is the largest group in the society
members are paid for their work at home
questions.explanation: Close, caring and lasting relationships make the family a primary group.

questions.stem: In a typical Nigerian family, one major responsibility of parents is to
options: do their children's school assignments every day
allow children to make all family decisions
provide food, shelter, education and moral training for their children
leave all moral training to the school
questions.explanation: Parents provide for children's needs and give them moral training.

questions.stem: Which of these is a role of children in the family?
options: Respecting parents and helping with house chores
Making major decisions for the family
questions.explanation: Children contribute by obeying parents and helping at home.

questions.topic: Consequences of Large and Small Family Sizes
questions.stem: A family made up of a father, a mother and very few children is described as a
questions.explanation: A small family has few children.

questions.topic: Consequences of Large and Small Family Sizes
questions.stem: Which of the following is a likely consequence of a very large family with low income?
options: Each child will receive more attention
The family will save more money each year
Children may not all get good education and care
The family will need less food
questions.explanation: With many children and little income, resources are spread thin.

questions.topic: Consequences of Large and Small Family Sizes
questions.stem: One advantage of a small family size is that
options: the children are always lonely and unhappy
the parents must work harder for more money
the family needs more land for farming
parents can give each child better care and education
questions.explanation: With fewer children, parents can meet each child's needs better.

questions.topic: Consequences of Large and Small Family Sizes
questions.stem: How can large family sizes across a country affect the national economy?
options: It always leads to more savings and investment
It reduces the demand for food
It makes government spending on schools unnecessary
Rapid population growth may outpace jobs, schools and hospitals
questions.explanation: When population grows faster than resources, there is pressure on jobs and social services.

questions.stem: Marriage can be defined as
options: a legally and socially accepted union of husband and wife
a contract between a landlord and a tenant
an agreement between two families to trade together
a friendship between two people of the same age
questions.explanation: Marriage is a union recognised by law and society.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a purpose of marriage?
questions.explanation: One main purpose of marriage is to have and raise children.

questions.stem: Besides having children, marriage provides companionship, which means
options: husband and wife compete against each other
husband and wife avoid talking to each other
husband and wife support and keep each other company
husband and wife live in different towns
questions.explanation: Companionship is the love, support and friendship couples share.

questions.stem: Which of the following purposes of marriage relates to meeting economic needs?
options: Giving names to children at a naming ceremony
Husband and wife pooling their resources to provide for the home
questions.explanation: Couples work together and share resources to meet the family's economic needs.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a condition a person should meet before getting married?
questions.explanation: A person should be able to take care of a family financially before marriage.

questions.stem: Psychological fitness for marriage means that a person
options: has enough money to pay the bride price
has reached the legal age for voting
questions.explanation: Psychological fitness is emotional maturity and readiness.

questions.stem: One effect of getting married without being ready is
options: a more peaceful and stable home
questions.explanation: Lack of readiness often causes conflict, instability and divorce.

questions.stem: Children from homes where the parents have separated because of constant fights may suffer from
options: emotional problems and lack of proper care
better school performance in every case
too much attention from both parents
questions.explanation: Broken homes can leave children emotionally hurt and neglected.

questions.stem: Group behaviour refers to
options: the way one person acts alone in his room
the number of people in a town
the way people act when they are together in a group
the colour of a group's uniform
questions.explanation: Group behaviour is how people behave as members of a group.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of positive group behaviour?
options: A gang fight between two streets
Communal labour to clean the village stream
questions.explanation: Communal labour is constructive group behaviour that benefits all.

questions.stem: One benefit of belonging to a positive group is
questions.explanation: Positive groups give companionship, security and status.

questions.stem: A protest in which participants burn cars and loot shops is an example of
questions.explanation: Burning and looting harm the society; that is destructive (negative) group behaviour.

questions.stem: Which of these is the main difference between constructive and destructive group behaviour?
options: Destructive behaviour is always legal while constructive behaviour is illegal
Constructive behaviour involves more people than destructive behaviour
Constructive behaviour benefits society while destructive behaviour harms people and property
Constructive behaviour happens only in the city
questions.explanation: The difference lies in the effect: one builds up society, the other damages it.

questions.stem: Human trafficking is
options: moving people illegally in order to exploit them
the legal transfer of workers between jobs
the export of goods to other countries
the transfer of students to new schools
questions.explanation: Human trafficking is moving people, by force or deceit, in order to exploit them.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a factor that makes children and women vulnerable to trafficking?
questions.explanation: Poor families are more easily deceived with false promises of jobs.

questions.stem: Victims of human trafficking are often lured by
options: false promises of good jobs or education
questions.explanation: Traffickers deceive victims with promises of good jobs or schooling.

questions.stem: One consequence of human trafficking on the family is
options: increase in family income at all times
weakening of family love and influence
better education for the trafficked child
questions.explanation: Trafficking separates family members and weakens family bonds.

questions.stem: How does human trafficking lead to a loss of human resources for Nigeria?
options: It creates more jobs in Nigerian factories
It increases school enrolment in Nigeria
It raises the number of skilled workers
Victims miss education and become unproductive
questions.explanation: Trafficked youths miss education and skill training, so the nation loses their potential.

questions.stem: The Nigerian government agency established to fight human trafficking is
questions.explanation: NAPTIP is the National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons.

questions.stem: Which of these is a preventive measure against human trafficking?
options: Accepting job offers from strangers without checks
Sending children to unknown people in the city
Awareness campaigns about the tricks of traffickers
questions.explanation: Awareness campaigns teach people how to recognise and avoid traffickers.

questions.stem: Making and enforcing laws that punish traffickers helps to prevent human trafficking through
questions.explanation: Legislation means making laws; enforcing them discourages traffickers.

questions.stem: Which of the following measures attacks the ROOT cause of human trafficking?
options: Banning all travel by young people
Reducing poverty through education and skills acquisition
Arresting victims when they return home
questions.explanation: Poverty makes people vulnerable; education and skills reduce it.

questions.stem: Harmful traditional practices are
options: customs practised only in rural areas
customs that harm people's health or rights
questions.explanation: These are old customs that harm people's health or rights.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a harmful traditional practice?
questions.explanation: Marrying off young girls harms their health and education.

questions.stem: One consequence of early marriage for a young girl is
options: more time for play and leisure
questions.explanation: A girl's body is not ready for childbirth, which can cause serious complications.

questions.stem: Using children to beg for alms on the streets is harmful mainly because it
options: keeps them out of school and exposes them to danger
keeps them safe from crime and abuse
gives them good education and skills
questions.explanation: Child begging keeps children out of school and exposes them to abuse and accidents.

questions.stem: Female genital mutilation (female circumcision) is discouraged because it
options: makes girls less intelligent in school
is done only in big cities
is too expensive for most families
can cause severe bleeding and infection
questions.explanation: It has no health benefit and causes serious harm.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the MOST effective way to end harmful traditional practices in a community?
options: Educating families and enforcing laws against them
Leaving the matter to each family to decide
Keeping silent so as not to offend the elders
Allowing the customs to be practised secretly
questions.explanation: Education changes attitudes, and laws protect potential victims.

questions.topic: Promoting Peaceful Living in Our Society
questions.stem: Peace can be described as
options: a situation where people avoid each other completely
a period when the military controls the country
a state of calm and harmony without violence or conflict
the victory of one group over another in a conflict
questions.explanation: Peace is living together without violence, in harmony.

questions.topic: Promoting Peaceful Living in Our Society
questions.stem: A situation where there is no open fighting but people still distrust one another and tension remains is called
questions.explanation: Negative peace is the mere absence of fighting while tension remains.

questions.topic: Promoting Peaceful Living in Our Society
questions.stem: Positive peace exists when
options: one group defeats another in war
people stop fighting only because soldiers are present
there is justice, fairness and cooperation, not just the absence of fighting
questions.explanation: Positive peace includes fairness, justice and good relationships.

questions.topic: Promoting Peaceful Living in Our Society
questions.stem: One importance of peace in a society is that it
questions.explanation: Development thrives where there is peace.

questions.topic: Promoting Peaceful Living in Our Society
questions.stem: Two communities are quarrelling over farmland. Which of the following actions would BEST promote lasting peace?
options: Dialogue and fair settlement of the dispute by neutral mediators
Asking one community to leave the area by force
questions.explanation: Dialogue and fair mediation address the cause of conflict and promote lasting peace.

questions.stem: Socialization is the process by which
options: a person learns the ways of life of his society
a person makes many friends at school
questions.explanation: Socialization is learning how to live in one's society.

questions.stem: The first and most important agent of socialization is the
questions.explanation: A child first learns language, values and behaviour from the family.

questions.stem: A group of people of about the same age and interests who influence one another is called a
questions.explanation: Peer groups are friends of similar age who shape attitudes and behaviour.

questions.stem: Newspapers, radio, television and the internet act as agents of socialization by
options: replacing the family in raising children
spreading information and shaping people's ideas and values
making and enforcing laws for the state
questions.explanation: The mass media inform people and influence their attitudes.

questions.stem: Religious organisations contribute to socialization mainly by
options: providing employment for all their members
collecting taxes on behalf of the state
teaching moral values such as honesty and love for others
questions.explanation: Churches and mosques teach moral and spiritual values.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the main importance of socialization to the society?
options: It ensures that everybody has the same religion
It makes all members of society think alike
It removes the need for schools and families
It passes culture and values to the next generation
questions.explanation: Socialization keeps culture and values alive across generations.

questions.stem: In many Nigerian communities, age grades help to socialize young people by
options: keeping them away from community activities
teaching them to disobey their elders
giving them money for their personal use
giving them community duties and teaching discipline
questions.explanation: Age grades assign community duties and enforce discipline among their members.

questions.topic: Road Safety Club as an Agent of Socialization
questions.stem: The Road Safety Club in schools is mainly concerned with
questions.explanation: Road Safety Clubs educate young people about road safety.

questions.topic: Road Safety Club as an Agent of Socialization
questions.stem: Road Safety Clubs in Nigerian schools are supported by the
questions.explanation: The FRSC promotes Road Safety Clubs in schools.

questions.topic: Road Safety Club as an Agent of Socialization
questions.stem: How does the Road Safety Club act as an agent of socialization?
options: It encourages members to enforce traffic fines
It trains members to become motor mechanics
It teaches members how to drive at high speed
It teaches members safe road habits and discipline
questions.explanation: The club passes on road safety values and good habits.

questions.topic: Road Safety Club as an Agent of Socialization
questions.stem: Which of the following activities would a school Road Safety Club MOST likely carry out?
options: Helping pupils to cross the road safely at the school gate
Arresting drivers who break traffic rules
Collecting fines from drivers on the highway
questions.explanation: Club members assist with safe crossing and road safety campaigns; enforcement belongs to officials.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a common social problem in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Unemployment is a serious social problem in Nigeria.

questions.stem: Kidnapping, armed robbery and cultism are examples of social problems related to
questions.explanation: These crimes create insecurity in society.

questions.stem: One major cause of corruption as a social problem in Nigeria is
options: greed and the desire to get rich quickly
questions.explanation: Greed and quick-money desires encourage corruption.

questions.stem: A town has many school-leavers without jobs, and cases of theft and drug use are rising. The social problem that is most likely the main cause is
questions.explanation: Idle, unemployed youths may turn to crime and drugs.

questions.topic: Ways of Solving Social Problems in Nigeria
questions.stem: Which of the following is an effect of social problems on a nation?
questions.explanation: Social problems slow down development.

questions.topic: Ways of Solving Social Problems in Nigeria
questions.stem: Government can reduce unemployment among youths by
options: providing skills training and small business loans
reducing the number of schools and colleges
questions.explanation: Skills training and business support create jobs.

questions.topic: Ways of Solving Social Problems in Nigeria
questions.stem: Which of these is a way individuals can help solve social problems?
options: Being honest and law-abiding in their daily lives
questions.explanation: Every citizen can help by practising good values.

questions.topic: Ways of Solving Social Problems in Nigeria
questions.stem: Which of the following approaches is most likely to reduce corruption in public offices on a long-term basis?
options: Reducing the powers of the courts
Increasing the number of public holidays
Allowing officials to keep secret accounts
questions.explanation: Strong institutions, openness and consistent punishment discourage corruption.

questions.topic: Our Roles in Promoting Safety in Our Community
questions.stem: Safety means
options: being protected from danger, injury or harm
questions.explanation: Safety is freedom from danger or harm.

questions.topic: Our Roles in Promoting Safety in Our Community
questions.stem: Pedestrians should cross the road
options: at a zebra crossing after looking left and right
questions.explanation: Using zebra crossings or bridges and looking carefully keeps pedestrians safe.

questions.topic: Our Roles in Promoting Safety in Our Community
questions.stem: A motorcyclist should always wear
questions.explanation: A crash helmet protects the head in case of an accident.

questions.topic: Our Roles in Promoting Safety in Our Community
questions.stem: Which of the following is a safety measure in the home?
options: Keeping medicines and chemicals out of the reach of children
Leaving gas cylinders open after cooking
questions.explanation: Children can be poisoned by medicines and chemicals left within reach.

questions.topic: Our Roles in Promoting Safety in Our Community
questions.stem: Using a mobile phone while driving is dangerous because it
questions.explanation: Phone use takes the driver's attention away from the road.

questions.topic: Our Roles in Promoting Safety in Our Community
questions.stem: In a workplace such as a carpentry workshop, which of the following is the BEST safety practice?
options: Allowing children to play near the machines
Leaving sharp tools on the floor after use
Wearing goggles and gloves when using machines
Operating machines while wearing loose clothing
questions.explanation: Protective equipment reduces the risk of injury at work.

questions.topic: Our Roles in Promoting Safety in Our Community
questions.stem: Why should cyclists wear bright or reflective clothing when riding at dusk?
options: Because it is the latest fashion trend
So that motorists can see them clearly
So that they can ride without lights
Because it makes the bicycle move faster
questions.explanation: Visibility helps other road users to notice cyclists in poor light.

questions.stem: Drug trafficking means
options: selling approved medicines in a registered pharmacy
a doctor prescribing drugs to a patient
the illegal production, transport and sale of hard drugs
questions.explanation: Drug trafficking is the illegal trade in dangerous drugs.

questions.stem: The agency responsible for fighting drug trafficking in Nigeria is the
questions.explanation: NDLEA arrests and prosecutes drug traffickers.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a reason some people engage in drug trafficking?
options: A wish to protect young people
Greed and the desire to make quick money
questions.explanation: Greed, poverty and ignorance push some people into drug trafficking.

questions.stem: One danger of drug trafficking to Nigeria is that it
options: gives the country a bad image abroad
questions.explanation: When Nigerians are caught trafficking drugs, the country's image suffers.

questions.stem: Which of the following coping skills would BEST help a student to say no when a friend offers him drugs?
questions.explanation: Assertiveness helps a person to firmly refuse what is harmful.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a constructive way young people can use their free time to stay away from drugs?
options: Hanging around motor parks at night
Taking part in sports and club activities
questions.explanation: Healthy activities keep youths busy and away from drugs.

questions.stem: Which of the following can help to prevent drug trafficking?
options: Education about the dangers of drugs
questions.explanation: Education helps people understand and avoid drug trafficking.

questions.stem: Drug traffickers who are convicted in Nigeria may lose the property they bought with drug money. This is called
questions.explanation: Forfeiture means the government takes away property gained through crime.

questions.stem: Reducing poverty helps to prevent drug trafficking because
options: rich people never break the law
drugs are sold only in villages
poverty tempts some people into the drug trade
poor people are the only ones who use drugs
questions.explanation: When people have decent means of livelihood, they are less tempted by drug money.

questions.stem: Why is cooperation with the international community important in preventing drug trafficking?
options: Cooperation increases foreign aid for drugs
Drugs are produced only in Nigeria
Other countries make Nigeria's drug laws
questions.explanation: Traffickers move drugs across countries, so nations must cooperate to stop them.

questions.topic: Meaning and Consequences of Drug Abuse and Harmful Substances
questions.stem: Drug abuse means
options: keeping drugs in a cool, dry place
misusing drugs or taking them without prescription
selling approved drugs in a pharmacy
questions.explanation: Drug abuse is the misuse of drugs or harmful substances.

questions.topic: Meaning and Consequences of Drug Abuse and Harmful Substances
questions.stem: Which of the following is a harmful substance commonly abused by some young people?
questions.explanation: Cannabis is a harmful substance that is illegal in Nigeria.

questions.topic: Meaning and Consequences of Drug Abuse and Harmful Substances
questions.stem: Taking cough syrup containing codeine in large quantities to 'get high' is an example of
questions.explanation: Using a medicine for a purpose other than treatment is drug abuse.

questions.topic: Meaning and Consequences of Drug Abuse and Harmful Substances
questions.stem: One effect of drug abuse on the individual is
options: damage to the brain, liver and other organs
questions.explanation: Drugs harm vital organs and can cause mental illness.

questions.topic: Meaning and Consequences of Drug Abuse and Harmful Substances
questions.stem: How does drug abuse among youths affect the community?
options: It increases the number of skilled workers
It increases crime, violence and loss of productive manpower
It reduces the need for hospitals
questions.explanation: Drug abusers may turn to crime and cannot contribute fully to the community.

questions.topic: Meaning and Consequences of Drug Abuse and Harmful Substances
questions.stem: Which of the following signs may indicate that a student is abusing drugs?
options: Active participation in sports and clubs
Sudden poor grades, red eyes and withdrawal
questions.explanation: Changes in behaviour, health and school work can be warning signs of drug abuse.

questions.topic: History of Nigerian Social Studies Education
questions.stem: Social Studies in Nigeria is best described as a subject that studies
options: the movement of planets and stars in space
the structure and functions of living cells
the history of ancient empires outside Africa
man and his relationship with his physical and social environment
questions.explanation: Social Studies is the study of man in his environment.

questions.stem: By teaching students about people from different parts of Nigeria, Social Studies helps to achieve the objective of
questions.explanation: Learning about other groups builds understanding and national unity.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a skill students develop through Social Studies?
questions.explanation: Map reading is one of the skills learnt in Social Studies.

questions.topic: Consequences of Large and Small Family Sizes
questions.stem: A family with a father, a mother and eight children is an example of a
questions.explanation: Many children make a large family.

questions.stem: In Nigeria, the three common types of marriage recognised are
options: federal, state and local government marriages
questions.explanation: Marriages may be customary, religious (church or Islamic) or statutory (court/registry).

questions.stem: Physical fitness for marriage means that a person
options: has enough money to start a family
has reached physical maturity and is in good health
questions.explanation: A person should be physically mature and healthy before marriage.

questions.stem: Parents can help prevent their children from being trafficked by
options: sending their children to live with unknown people
encouraging children to travel alone at night
refusing to hand their children to strangers who promise jobs abroad
keeping their children out of school
questions.explanation: Parents should not give their children to people they do not know well.

questions.topic: Promoting Peaceful Living in Our Society
questions.stem: Which of the following values is most important for promoting peaceful living among people of different religions?
questions.explanation: Tolerance means accepting and respecting other people's beliefs.

questions.topic: Promoting Peaceful Living in Our Society
questions.stem: Social justice promotes peace in a society because
options: people feel they are treated fairly and equally
only the rich are protected by the law
some groups are denied their rights
questions.explanation: When people feel fairly treated, there is less cause for conflict.

questions.topic: Road Safety Club as an Agent of Socialization
questions.stem: Which of the following is a step in forming a Road Safety Club in a school?
options: Recruiting only adults from outside the school
Getting the school's approval and a teacher-patron
Buying a car for members to learn driving
Collecting road tolls from passing motorists
questions.explanation: A school club needs approval from the school and a teacher to guide it.

questions.stem: The illegal transport of goods across a country's border without paying customs duty is called
questions.explanation: Smuggling is a social and economic problem that cheats the government of revenue.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a cause of the social problem of armed robbery?
questions.explanation: Idleness and greed can lead young people into armed robbery.

questions.topic: Ways of Solving Social Problems in Nigeria
questions.stem: Which of the following measures can help to reduce cultism in schools?
options: Counselling students and enforcing school rules
Ignoring secret meetings on the school compound
Allowing cult members to become prefects
questions.explanation: Guidance and firm discipline discourage cultism.

questions.topic: Ways of Solving Social Problems in Nigeria
questions.stem: Why is good governance important in solving social problems in Nigeria?
options: It increases the level of corruption
Good governance means having no laws at all
It makes citizens depend on bribes
Public resources are used to provide jobs and services
questions.explanation: Accountable leaders invest public funds in things that reduce poverty and crime.

questions.stem: A woman promised Ada's parents that she would take Ada to Lagos to attend school, but instead made her a house help without pay or schooling. Ada is a victim of
questions.explanation: Taking a child away by deceit and exploiting her labour is trafficking and child labour.

questions.stem: The school acts as an agent of socialization by
options: teaching knowledge, skills and rules for living together
questions.explanation: Schools teach knowledge, skills, discipline and how to live with others.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a secondary group rather than a primary group?
options: A small circle of close friends
questions.explanation: Secondary groups like trade unions are large and formal with less personal relationships.

questions.stem: Acting patriotically, such as joining others to clean up after a flood, is a group behaviour that mainly brings
questions.explanation: Positive group action helps a community achieve common goals.

questions.topic: Meaning and Consequences of Drug Abuse and Harmful Substances
questions.stem: Which of the following is a form of drug abuse?
options: Completing a course of antibiotics as directed
